reason: Fixes a cluster of Mission-run and shared automation-runtime recovery defects (audit MIS-1..MIS-6) plus the last unpaged AgentRun lookup in missions.py. MIS-1: specialists record their routing response on the attempt before brokering and replay it on restart instead of re-asking the model; invocation ids/idempotency keys derive from (run, task, turn, position) not the provider's random call id; a slot the broker refuses becomes an explicit unknown observation. MIS-2: AutomationBroker refuses a RUNNING/FAILED/CANCELLED/DENIED ledger row without a trustworthy receipt (AmbiguousToolState), re-entering only from WAITING_APPROVAL with a durable decision, which also protects chat/harness command continuations. MIS-3: Mission run_command approvals route to the mission service and resume the run; the card is bound to its tool call and task and rebuilt from the durable ledger row. MIS-4: cancelling the task awaiting a foreground command terminates the process and records it cancelled. MIS-5: restart-recovery events are keyed by a per-cycle generation. MIS-6: a CANCELLING run is finalized as cancelled on restart, not resurrected. Selected: the mission lifecycle/recovery/approval suite; the specialist orchestration, batch-routing and routing-tolerance suites; the automation runtime/broker suite; the tool-failure envelope suite (unknown-outcome observation); the background results webhook suite; the row-horizon guard, which now enforces missions.py after this PR removes the last exemption; and the generic CRUD exposure guard (AgentAttempt gains a field, no new kind). MIS-4 is reconciled with #572 (HARN-5): one foreground-cancel implementation using #569's stop-status rule; this PR adds the MIS-4 test and a shielded finalizer on process_io terminate.
exclusions: Full suites are not approved and are excluded. tests/v3/test_automation_runtime.py::test_host_scope_expiry_closes_running_commands is a pre-existing load-sensitive timing flake (0.5s scope expiry + 0.8s assertion) that fails identically on pristine origin/main under heavy concurrent load and is unrelated to this change. No UI, Playwright, native Rust/Tauri, or migration changes: AgentAttempt gains a defaulted nullable routing_response field inside existing JSON payloads (old rows validate; no schema change), and the live DB has zero Mission runs.
